2013-08-19: Ted Cruz says he will renounce any Canadian citizenship after a report that he may be a dual citizen of the USA and Canada.
2013-09-24: Ted Cruz spoke from 2:40pm ET Tuesday to 12:03pm ET Wednesday in a faux-filibuster against Obamacare.
2013-09-26: Ted Cruz is described as driving the Republican Party's strategy tying the budget and debt limit to defunding or delaying Obamacare, leading to a possible government shutdown.
2013-09-27: Ted Cruz led 19 Republican senators in voting against a procedural motion to advance a spending bill, after which the Senate stripped out the Obamacare defunding clause and sent the bill back to the House.
2013-10-05: Ted Cruz emerges as a leading figure in the Republican strategy over Obamacare that prompted a US government shutdown, acting as an unofficial envoy between House conservatives and the Senate.
2013-10-12: Ted Cruz is cited as evidence that gerrymandering did not cause increased political polarization, since he was elected to the Senate in a statewide election where redistricting does not apply.
2013-12-29: Ted Cruz said he is taking steps to renounce his Canadian citizenship.
2014-03-04: Ted Cruz's refusal to endorse Senator John Cornyn for re-election and his anti-establishment stance are cited as driving Texas Republican primary candidates to the right ahead of voting.
2014-06-03: Ted Cruz won the straw poll at the Republican Leadership Conference in New Orleans after giving an anti-establishment speech.
2014-08-08: Ted Cruz spoke at the RedState Gathering conservative convention, where he reiterated admiration for Rick Perry and deflected but did not dismiss questions about a possible 2016 presidential run.
2014-11-20: Senator Ted Cruz delivered a Senate floor speech denouncing President Obama's planned executive action on immigration, adapting remarks by Cicero to accuse Obama of wanting to "destroy the constitution."
2015-01-12: Senator Ted Cruz is appointed to chair the subcommittee overseeing science and NASA in the new Republican-controlled Congress.
2015-02-26: Ted Cruz delivered a pugilistic speech at CPAC, attacking the political establishment on both the left and right and outlining his agenda for a potential presidency.
2015-03-23: Ted Cruz announces his candidacy for the 2016 Republican presidential nomination with a speech at Liberty University in Virginia.
Ted Cruz raised $4.3 million in his first week as a presidential candidate, outpacing Mitt Romney's early 2012 fundraising.
2015-04-25: Republican presidential candidate Ted Cruz said conservatives should “fall to our knees and pray” that the Supreme Court will not make same-sex marriage legal in all 50 states.
2015-04-26: Gay hotelier Ian Reisner apologized to the LGBT community for hosting a “fireside chat” with Republican presidential candidate Ted Cruz, calling it “a terrible mistake.”
2015-06-30: Ted Cruz said Chief Justice John Roberts "violated his oath" when he backed Obamacare in a Supreme Court decision.
2015-08-02: Republican presidential candidate Ted Cruz expressed "full out denial" of global warming during a forum hosted by Freedom Partners.
2015-09-19: Ted Cruz spoke at the Mackinac Republican Leadership Conference, making jokes about Democratic candidates and outlining conservative policy promises.
2015-09-28: Ted Cruz was abandoned by his colleagues in a Senate vote to advance a bipartisan spending bill, after which he spoke angrily for an hour to a near-empty chamber, accusing Republican leadership of abdicating its responsibility to fight for conservative principles.
2015-11-13: Republican presidential candidate Ted Cruz unveiled a hardline immigration plan that would limit legal immigration, increase deportations, end birthright citizenship, and build a wall along the US-Mexico border.
2015-11-28: Ted Cruz became the first Republican presidential candidate to directly address the fatal shooting at a Planned Parenthood clinic in Colorado, calling the attack "horrific" and "unacceptable."
2015-12-02: Ted Cruz condemned campus protesters at Princeton University as "pampered teenagers" over their campaign to remove Woodrow Wilson's name from the Wilson School of Public and International Affairs.
2015-12-10: Ted Cruz rejected calls from fellow Republicans to revive mass telephone surveillance after the San Bernardino terrorist attack, arguing that bulk data collection had failed to detect the plotters.
2015-12-12: A Bloomberg/Des Moines Register poll shows Ted Cruz leading the Republican field in Iowa with 31% support, ahead of Donald Trump at 21%.
2015-12-25: Ted Cruz begins his #CruzCountryChristmasTour, traveling across the country by private jet.
2016-01-05: Donald Trump cast doubt on Ted Cruz's eligibility for the presidency, claiming Cruz may not be a natural-born US citizen because he was born in Canada.
2016-01-10: Ted Cruz insists he is a natural-born citizen and dismisses claims from Donald Trump and other Republicans that he is not qualified to be president.

Harvard law professor Laurence Tribe says the legal and constitutional issues around whether Ted Cruz is a “natural-born citizen” eligible for the presidency are “murky and unsettled,” a position cited by Donald Trump in his attacks on Cruz.
2016-01-12: Ted Cruz released a commercial titled “Invasion” in New Hampshire in which he says that if elected president he will triple the border patrol, build a wall “that works,” and secure the border.
2016-01-14: At a Republican debate in South Carolina, Ted Cruz responded to Donald Trump's claim that he is not "natural-born" and thus ineligible for the presidency, arguing that under Trump's citizenship logic Trump himself would be disqualified.

During a Republican debate, Ted Cruz called Harvard law professor Laurence Tribe a "leftwing judicial activist" after Donald Trump cited Tribe in questioning Cruz's eligibility to be president, despite Cruz having cited Tribe in his own Supreme Court briefs.
2016-01-20: A CNN/WMUR poll shows Donald Trump widening his lead over Ted Cruz to 20 points among Republicans likely to vote in the New Hampshire primary.
2016-01-23: Ted Cruz challenges Donald Trump to a one-on-one debate in Iowa and offers a $1.5 million donation to veterans' organizations if Trump accepts.
2016-01-26: Ted Cruz campaigned in Iowa ahead of the state's caucuses, telling voters he is the real conservative and sharply criticizing Donald Trump.
2016-01-30: Ted Cruz delivered a dystopian vision of America’s future ahead of the Iowa caucuses, warning that other Republicans would put religious freedoms at risk and that the nation was one Supreme Court justice away from abortion on demand and the removal of religious symbols from memorials.
Iowa Secretary of State Paul Pate formally condemned the Cruz campaign for sending mailers that falsely accused voters of a "voting violation," and Cruz responded by refusing to apologize.
2016-02-01: Donald Trump claims Ted Cruz committed fraud in winning the Republican Iowa caucuses and calls for a new election.
Ted Cruz wins the Iowa Republican caucuses, beating Donald Trump.
2016-02-03: Ben Carson held a press conference to criticize Ted Cruz for his campaign spreading rumors that Carson was dropping out of the race on the night of the Iowa caucuses, though Carson refused to name Cruz directly.
2016-02-04: Canadians, particularly Albertans, disavow Ted Cruz after his victory in the Republican Iowa caucus, rejecting his association with Canada and expressing disapproval of his politics.
2016-02-15: Donald Trump threatened to sue Ted Cruz over his eligibility and the "lies" recited by his campaign, while Cruz responded with attacks on Trump.
2016-02-16: Ted Cruz touted his national security credentials on a statewide tour in South Carolina, pledging to increase US army enlistment by 75,000 troops and add more ships and planes.
2016-02-17: Senators Ted Cruz and Marco Rubio are among the Republican obstructionists who want to block Obama from nominating a new US supreme court justice.
Ted Cruz dared Donald Trump to sue him over a negative campaign ad, saying he would welcome a lawsuit and that Trump's own words on national television cannot be defamation.
2016-02-21: Ted Cruz and Marco Rubio campaigned in Nevada, each arguing they are the most viable challenger to Donald Trump for the Republican presidential nomination.
2016-02-22: Ted Cruz fired national spokesman Rick Tyler after Tyler promoted a false story questioning Marco Rubio's commitment to the Bible.
2016-02-23: Ted Cruz's presidential campaign is described as flailing after Donald Trump's third resounding victory, with Cruz pinning his hopes on his home state of Texas ahead of Super Tuesday.
2016-03-02: A "Ted Cruz is the Zodiac killer" meme-inspired T-shirt fundraising project ended sales after selling about 7,500 shirts, raising an estimated $69,000 for the West Fund.
2016-03-05: Ted Cruz wins the Republican caucuses in Kansas and Maine.
2016-03-07: Ted Cruz campaigned in Mississippi and Michigan ahead of their votes the next day, reportedly preparing to announce his first endorsements from Senate colleagues.
2016-03-12: Ted Cruz took an early lead in the Wyoming Republican caucuses and picked up a single delegate in Guam's Republican primary.
2016-03-22: Ted Cruz won the Utah Republican caucus with more than 50% of the vote, securing all 40 of the state's delegates.
2016-03-23: Jeb Bush endorses Ted Cruz for the Republican presidential nomination, following Cruz's victory in the Utah primary.

Donald Trump and Ted Cruz traded Twitter barbs over their wives' honor after an anti-Trump group ran Facebook ads featuring a nearly-nude photo of Melania Trump, with Trump accusing Cruz's campaign of being behind the picture and Cruz denying it and warning Trump not to attack Heidi Cruz.
2016-03-25: Ted Cruz held a press conference to call a tabloid story alleging he had extramarital affairs "lies" and a "smear" from Donald Trump and his "henchmen," while Trump denied having anything to do with the story.
2016-03-28: Wisconsin Governor Scott Walker endorsed Ted Cruz for the Republican presidential nomination.
2016-04-02: Ted Cruz detoured from campaigning in Wisconsin to appear at North Dakota's Republican convention, where presidential delegates were being picked.
2016-04-06: Ted Cruz emerges as the main rival to Donald Trump and a safer bet for the Republican establishment despite longstanding party misgivings.
2016-04-08: Ted Cruz picked up 12 more delegates in Colorado, giving him 21 of the state's 37 delegates ahead of the state convention.
2016-04-09: The Trump campaign's ballot error at the Colorado state convention may lead voters to support Ted Cruz delegates.
Ted Cruz won all 34 delegates available in Colorado, including the final 13 at the state convention, continuing his dominance in the state's Republican delegate selection process.
2016-04-13: A report highlights that Ted Cruz, as Texas solicitor general in 2007, helped defend Texas's ban on the sale of sex toys in a federal court case.
2016-04-19: Donald Trump wins the New York Republican primary, decisively defeating Ted Cruz and undoing the delegate gains Cruz made after his Wisconsin victory.
2016-04-20: Ted Cruz predicted that the Republican presidential race would culminate in a contested convention after Donald Trump won over 60% of the New York Republican primary vote.
2016-04-22: Maine Governor Paul LePage accused Ted Cruz’s campaign of reneging on a delegate unity deal and condemned it as run by “greedy political hooligans.”
2016-04-24: Ted Cruz and John Kasich announce a deal in which Cruz will focus resources on Indiana while Kasich focuses on Oregon and New Mexico, in an attempt to prevent Donald Trump from reaching the 1,237 delegates needed to clinch the Republican nomination.
2016-05-01: Ted Cruz made a series of last-ditch attacks on Donald Trump ahead of the Indiana primary, calling him corrupt and part of a political "cartel" with Hillary Clinton.
2016-05-03: Ted Cruz dropped out of the presidential race after a disastrous loss in Indiana.
2016-05-07: Ted Cruz ends his campaign for the presidency.
2016-05-10: Ted Cruz refused to commit his support to Donald Trump as the Republican nominee and did not rule out resurrecting his presidential campaign despite having dropped out of the race.
2016-05-14: Ted Cruz returned to the Republican stage at the Texas state convention, avoiding mention of Donald Trump while telling Texans he would continue fighting for a far-right conservative movement.
2016-07-20: Ted Cruz was showered with boos at the Republican national convention after he withheld his endorsement of Donald Trump as the Republican nominee.
2016-07-21: Ted Cruz refused to endorse Donald Trump at the Republican convention and told Texas delegates he is not "a servile puppy dog" to Trump.
2016-09-23: Ted Cruz announced on Facebook that he will vote for Republican nominee Donald Trump, citing his promise to support the nominee and his opposition to Hillary Clinton.
2016-09-24: Ted Cruz refuses to say Donald Trump is fit to be president after endorsing him, citing Hillary Clinton as unfit and a binary choice.
2016-11-01: Republican Senator Ted Cruz voiced support for indefinitely blocking any Supreme Court nominee proposed by Hillary Clinton if she were elected, breaking with 150-year precedent.
2017-09-24: Ted Cruz says he will not vote for the Graham-Cassidy healthcare bill in its current form and believes Mike Lee will also oppose it.
